prompt: The DaemonSet `node-agent` has no `replicas`. How many pods did it run on the three-node cluster?

choices.text: Three, one per node
choices.why: The control-plane node's taint kept it off, and the DaemonSet does not tolerate it.

choices.text: Two, one per worker
choices.why: Right. Every node that may run it gets one, and the control plane may not.

choices.text: One, as a default replica count
choices.why: A DaemonSet has no count; it follows the nodes.

choices.text: As many as the scheduler chooses
choices.why: The question a DaemonSet asks is which nodes, not how many.

prompt: A fourth node joins the cluster. What happens to the DaemonSet `node-agent`?

choices.text: Nothing until somebody raises a replica count
choices.why: There is no count to raise; that is a Deployment's model.

choices.text: One existing pod moves to the new node
choices.why: Pods never move; the existing ones stay where they are.

choices.text: The new node gets a pod of its own straight away
choices.why: Right, as long as no taint keeps it off.

choices.text: The new node is skipped until the DaemonSet is applied again
choices.why: The controller watches nodes; nobody has to apply anything.

prompt: With `completions: 3` and `parallelism: 2`, why did the third `report` pod start later than the other two?
hint: How many may run at the same time?

choices.text: It waited for one of the first two to finish
choices.why: Right: never more than two at once, three successes in all.

choices.text: The first attempt at it failed
choices.why: All three pods ended `Completed`; nothing failed.

choices.text: The scheduler had no room on the workers
choices.why: The workers were nearly idle; the limit was the Job's own.

choices.text: Jobs always start their pods one at a time
choices.why: Two started together, as `parallelism: 2` allows.

prompt: The Job `broken` has `backoffLimit: 2`. How many pods did it make before it gave up?
hint: The first attempt, then the retries.

prompt: A nightly migration Job fails. A pipeline must decide whether to alert. Which part of the Job should it read?
hint: The reason the Job gave up.

choices.text: The number of pods with `Error` status
choices.why: That counts attempts, and a Job can succeed after some of them fail.

choices.text: The exit code printed in the logs of the first pod
choices.why: The first pod may be a failure that a later retry fixed.

choices.text: Its `Failed` condition and reason
choices.why: Right: `BackoffLimitExceeded` says the Job as a whole has given up.

choices.text: How long the Job has existed
choices.why: Age says nothing about success.

prompt: A CronJob without `timeZone` has the schedule `0 2 * * *`. On most clusters, when does it run?

choices.text: At 02:00 in the time zone of the person who applied it
choices.why: Nothing records where the person was; the cluster reads the schedule.

choices.text: At 02:00 UTC
choices.why: Right: the controller manager's time zone, usually UTC, which is 23:00 in São Paulo.

choices.text: At 02:00 in the time zone of each node
choices.why: One controller decides when to make the Job, not every node.

choices.text: Every two hours
choices.why: `0 2 * * *` is minute 0 of hour 2, once a day.

prompt: The CronJob's second Job was named `nightly-29855110`. What is that number?

choices.text: A random suffix, like a pod's
choices.why: It is one more than the previous run's, a minute later.

choices.text: A count of how many times it has run
choices.why: It had run twice.

choices.text: A hash of the job template
choices.why: A hash would not grow by one each minute.

choices.text: The scheduled time, in minutes since 1970
choices.why: Right: 17:10 UTC on 6 October 2026, which is what the run printed.

hint: Ask: every node, to completion, or on a schedule?

pairs.left: A log collector on every machine
A database migration that runs once
